title: Roast lamb chops with marrow and chickpeas

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or basic staple: marrow, onions, tinned chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, lamb chops, Greek yoghurt, herbs and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a Tesco staple; eight lamb chops cost more than most dinners but are not a specialist buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a small bowl and a knife, with simple tray-roasting technique.

works.reason: Roasting the marrow first drives off its water, and 15 minutes at 220°C cooks the chops through, with sensible amounts for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers peeling and chunking the marrow, wedging two onions and chopping the mint, and the 40 minutes of cooking matches the 25 plus 15 in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the third tablespoon of oil for the chops and the pepper in 'seasoned', is used, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Marrow is the main vegetable of an August tray roast with mint and tomatoes, which suits the date.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British English with no restaurant jargon or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a balanced family dinner of lamb, chickpeas and vegetables with a yoghurt sauce.
